mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a tangent to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of contact?

options.A: The tangent is parallel to the radius
options.B: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius
options.C: The tangent makes a 45° angle with the radius
options.D: The tangent coincides with the radius

mcqs.answer: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius
mcqs.explanation: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. The radius drawn to that point of contact is always perpendicular to the tangent. Hence option B is correct; the other options contradict the tangent‑radius theorem.

mcqs.question: From a point A outside a circle with centre O, OA = 13 cm and the radius of the circle is 5 cm. What is the length of the tangent drawn from A to the circle?
mcqs.explanation: In triangle OAP, OA is the hypotenuse, OP = radius = 5 cm, and AP is the tangent. By the Pythagorean theorem, AP = √(OA²‑OP²) = √(13²‑5²) = √144 = 12 cm. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line l touches the circle at exactly one point P, while line m cuts the circle at two points Q and R. Which line is a tangent to the circle?
mcqs.explanation: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. Line l meets this definition, whereas line m intersects the circle at two points, making it a secant. Therefore, option A is correct.

mcqs.question: A point P lies on a circle with centre O. A line through P is drawn such that it does not intersect the circle at any other point. How would you define this line?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent. It is not a secant (which meets the circle at two points), a diameter (which passes through the centre), or a chord (which has both endpoints on the circle). Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: If a line touches a circle at point T, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The line intersects the circle at two points
options.B: The line is perpendicular to the radius OT at T
options.C: The line passes through the centre of the circle
options.D: The line is a chord of the circle

mcqs.answer: The line is perpendicular to the radius OT at T
mcqs.explanation: A tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact. At that point, the radius drawn to T is perpendicular to the tangent. Options A, C, and D describe other types of lines, not a tangent.

mcqs.question: Why must the radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent be perpendicular to the tangent line?

options.A: Because the tangent is the longest possible line from the centre to the circle
options.B: Because the shortest distance from a point to a line is along the perpendicular, and a tangent touches the circle at only one point
options.C: Because the centre, point of contact, and any other point on the tangent are collinear
options.D: Because the tangent and radius are parallel by definition

mcqs.answer: Because the shortest distance from a point to a line is along the perpendicular, and a tangent touches the circle at only one point
mcqs.explanation: The radius connects the centre to the point of contact. The shortest distance from the centre to the tangent line is the perpendicular distance; if the line were not perpendicular, it would intersect the circle at another point, contradicting the definition of a tangent. Hence option B correctly explains the theorem.

mcqs.question: Two external points P and Q are each connected to a circle with centre O. From P a tangent PT is drawn, and from Q a tangent QS is drawn. Which of the following statements is always true?

options.A: PT = QS only if OP = OQ
options.B: PT = QS regardless of the positions of P and Q

mcqs.explanation: The length of a tangent from an external point equals √(OP²‑r²). If OP > OQ, then √(OP²‑r²) > √(OQ²‑r²), so PT > QS. Option C captures this relationship; the other options are false in general.

mcqs.question: From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle, and a secant PCD cuts the circle at C and D. Which relation is always correct?
mcqs.explanation: Tangents drawn from the same external point to a circle are equal in length, so PA = PB. While the power of a point gives PA·PB = PC·PD, the equality of the two tangents is the direct and always‑true relation asked. Hence option A is correct.
